items.note: Between-subjects experiment with 45 design students comparing self-reflection, written stepwise guidance, and an antagonistic AI agent while revising design proposals; outcomes are self-rated reconsideration, counts of proposal improvements and of ideas generated and discarded, with no rated creativity in the abstract; below 50 participants.

Two-section quasi-experiment in an undergraduate illustration studio (Midjourney ideation workflow n = 82 vs conventional workflow n = 80) with expert-rated originality, appropriateness, elaboration, and a homogenisation measure on final artefacts; assignment is by class section, not random.

System paper on a GAN-based sketch-to-image art co-creation tool, evaluated with 60 art students against traditional tools on expert-judged creative output quality; the comparison design is not described, and a GAN tool may fall outside the generative-AI scope.

AEA RCT registry entry (AEARCTR-0016016), not a paper: individuals randomized via Qualtrics to ChatGPT-assisted or independent business idea generation, with idea quality and evaluation outcomes; 200 is the planned sample, and no results paper was found.

Undergraduate research journal article: 33 students randomly assigned to brainstorm with ChatGPT or alone before writing poems, which were ranked for creativity and coded for strategies and unique words; below 50 participants.

Experiment comparing a scaffolded LLM tool (Supermind Ideator), plain ChatGPT, and working alone on creative problem solving, with idea innovativeness as the outcome; N and assignment are not in the abstract; ACM CI 2024 version (10.1145/3643562.3672611) and arXiv 2311.01937 are related records.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC, Springer page); search notes describe two experiments varying the emotional valence and arousal of AI-generated inspirational images given to design learners, with rated design creativity, so all arms see AI images and it may be a stimulus study rather than AI assistance.

Controlled lab experiments with students and field tests with professional designers compare design work with and without GenAI at ideation and execution stages, with rated creativity; N and assignment are not in the abstract.

226 students using GenAI in problem-based learning were assigned to a critical-thinking intervention or a comparison condition (both used GenAI), with originality and idea density scored on group reports; the contrast is instruction around AI use rather than AI access, so the next stage should check whether it counts as a different AI configuration.

Two-class experiment (46 students) comparing generative-AI co-regulated learning with conventional co-regulated learning in digital game development projects; outcomes are project design performance and creative thinking, possibly self-reported; assignment appears to be by class, and the sample is below 50.
